```{r}
library(MASS)


data <- read.csv("student-mat.csv", sep=";")


data$schoolsup <- as.factor(data$schoolsup)


n <- nrow(data)
nt <- 300
neval <- n - nt
rep <- 5

errlin <- numeric(rep)
errqua <- numeric(rep)

set.seed(0607)

for(k in 1:rep){

  train <- sample(1:n, nt)

  ## linear discriminant analysis
  m1 <- lda(schoolsup ~ G1 + G2 + G3, data = data[train, ])
  tablin <- table(data$schoolsup[-train], predict(m1, data[-train, ])$class)
  errlin[k] <- (neval - sum(diag(tablin))) / neval

  ## quadratic discriminant analysis
  m2 <- qda(schoolsup ~ G1 + G2 + G3, data = data[train, ])
  tabqua <- table(data$schoolsup[-train], predict(m2, data[-train, ])$class)
  errqua[k] <- (neval - sum(diag(tabqua))) / neval
}

merrlin <- mean(errlin)
merrqua <- mean(errqua)


merrlin
merrqua
```
The linear discriminant analysis model has a smaller error rate than the quadratic discriminant analysis model. Therefore, the linear discriminant analysis performs better for this dataset.
